## Pulling files to the surface

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash -e
#SBATCH --account        massey03727
#SBATCH --job-name       dorado_demultiplex
#SBATCH --mem            20G
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task  16
#SBATCH --time           12:00:00
#SBATCH --output         dorado_demultiplex.out
#SBATCH --error          %x_%j.err

# purge any other modules loaded in the background to avoid conflicts, then load the required one
module purge
module load Dorado/1.4.0

BASE=/nesi/nobackup/massey03727/sequencing_runs_pod5
KIT=SQK-RBK114-24

RUNS=(
  01Aug24
  05Dec24
  07Nov24
  08Jul24
  1_12_05Sept24
  12Sept24
  13_24_05Sept24
  14Oct24
  15Aug24
  18Nov24
  23Sept24
  26Aug24
  29Jul24
)

# Moves demuxed files up out of the MinKNOW-style nested folders (e.g. pass/barcode01/*.bam)
# into a flat directory, prefixing filenames with their parent folder name to avoid collisions,
# then removes the now-empty subfolders.
flatten_demux() {
  local dir="$1"
  find "$dir" -mindepth 2 -type f -name "*.bam" | while read -r f; do
    parent=$(basename "$(dirname "$f")")
    mv "$f" "$dir/${parent}_$(basename "$f")"
  done
  find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -type d -empty -delete
}

for RUN in "${RUNS[@]}"; do
  BAM="${BASE}/${RUN}_methyl_calls.bam"
  OUT="${BASE}/${RUN}_barcodes"

  if [[ ! -f "$BAM" ]]; then
    echo "WARNING: $BAM not found, skipping $RUN" >&2
    continue
  fi

  echo "Demultiplexing $RUN..."
  dorado demux --kit-name "$KIT" --output-dir "$OUT" "$BAM"

  echo "Flattening output for $RUN..."
  flatten_demux "$OUT"
done

```

## SAMtools

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=bam2fastq
#SBATCH --account=massey03727
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --output=bam2fastq_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=bam2fastq_%j.err

module purge
module load SAMtools/1.23.1-GCC-12.3.0

PARENT_DIR="."   # directory containing the *_barcodes dirs

for dir in "${PARENT_DIR}"/*_barcodes/; do
    dir="${dir%/}"   # strip trailing slash
    dir_name=$(basename "${dir}")
    mapping_file="${dir}/${dir_name}.csv"

    echo "=== Processing directory: ${dir} ==="

    if [[ ! -f "${mapping_file}" ]]; then
        echo "  WARNING: no ${dir_name}.csv found inside ${dir}, skipping directory" >&2
        continue
    fi

    # read mapping file line by line: pattern,sample_name
    while IFS=',' read -r pattern sample_name; do
        # strip trailing carriage return / whitespace (common if CSV was
        # exported from Excel/Sheets on Windows)
        pattern="${pattern%$'\r'}"
        sample_name="${sample_name%$'\r'}"

        [[ -z "${pattern}" ]] && continue   # skip blank lines

        bam_file=$(find "${dir}" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "${pattern}.bam" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
        # also allow patterns that already include .bam in the CSV
        if [[ -z "${bam_file}" ]]; then
            bam_file=$(find "${dir}" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "${pattern}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
        fi

        if [[ -z "${bam_file}" ]]; then
            echo "  WARNING: no BAM matching '${pattern}' found in ${dir}, skipping" >&2
            continue
        fi

        out_fq="${dir}/${sample_name}.fq"

        echo "  ${bam_file} -> ${out_fq}"
        if ! samtools fastq -T '*' "${bam_file}" > "${out_fq}"; then
            echo "  ERROR: samtools fastq failed on ${bam_file}, continuing with next file" >&2
            rm -f "${out_fq}"   # remove any partial/empty output
            continue
        fi

    done < "${mapping_file}"

    echo
done

echo "Done. Renamed FASTQ files written alongside their source BAMs in each *_barcodes directory."

```


## Preparing csv files 

CSV files were generated to rename the barcodes to the isolate names per directory. There were 13 seperate directories, hence the check that all 13 of them have the renaming file. 

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash -e
#SBATCH --account massey03727
#SBATCH --job-name=test # job name (shows up in the queue)
#SBATCH --output=test_rename.log
#SBATCH --time=00:03:00 # Walltime (HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4 # number of cpus/threads, stick to 2 for now
#SBATCH --mem=4G            # RAM
#SBATCH --error         %x_%j.err

module purge

for d in *_barcodes/; do
    d="${d%/}"
    if [[ -f "${d}/${d}.csv" ]]; then
        echo "OK: ${d}"
    else
        echo "MISSING: ${d}/${d}.csv"
    fi
done
```


## Fastq files moved into one directory

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=collect_fastq
#SBATCH --account=massey03727
#SBATCH --time=00:30:00
#SBATCH --mem=2G
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --output=collect_fastq_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=collect_fastq_%j.err


PARENT_DIR="."
COMBINED_DIR="combined_fastq"
COPY_MODE="cp"   # change to "mv" to move instead of copy
PARALLEL_JOBS="${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK:-4}"

mkdir -p "${COMBINED_DIR}"

# Build a flat list of "source_path" for every .fq file across all directories
file_list=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "${file_list}"' EXIT

for dir in "${PARENT_DIR}"/*_barcodes/; do
    dir="${dir%/}"

    shopt -s nullglob
    fq_files=("${dir}"/*.fq)
    shopt -u nullglob

    if [[ ${#fq_files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "NOTE: no .fq files found in ${dir}, skipping"
        continue
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "${fq_files[@]}" >> "${file_list}"
done

total=$(wc -l < "${file_list}")
echo "Found ${total} .fq files to copy, using ${PARALLEL_JOBS} parallel workers"

# Warn (but don't block) on filename collisions before copying
sort -t/ -k2 <(xargs -I{} basename {} < "${file_list}") | uniq -d > /tmp/collision_check.$$
if [[ -s /tmp/collision_check.$$ ]]; then
    echo "WARNING: the following filenames appear in more than one source directory:" >&2
    cat /tmp/collision_check.$$ >&2
fi
rm -f /tmp/collision_check.$$

# Do the actual copy in parallel
xargs -a "${file_list}" -P "${PARALLEL_JOBS}" -I{} "${COPY_MODE}" {} "${COMBINED_DIR}/"

echo
echo "Done. ${total} .fq files placed in ${COMBINED_DIR}/"
```

## Filtlong

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=filtlong
#SBATCH --account=massey03727
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=8G
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --output=filtlong_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=filtlong_%j.err


module purge
module load Filtlong/0.2.0

INPUT_DIR="combined_fastq"
OUTPUT_DIR="filtered_fastq"
FILTLONG_OPTS="--min_length 1000 --keep_percent 90 --target_bases 500000000"

mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}"

shopt -s nullglob
fq_files=("${INPUT_DIR}"/*.fq)
shopt -u nullglob

if [[ ${#fq_files[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "ERROR: no .fq files found in ${INPUT_DIR}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

echo "Found ${#fq_files[@]} isolate FASTQ files in ${INPUT_DIR}"

for fq in "${fq_files[@]}"; do
    base=$(basename "${fq}" .fq)
    out_fq="${OUTPUT_DIR}/${base}_QC.fq"

    echo "Filtering ${fq} -> ${out_fq}"

    if ! filtlong ${FILTLONG_OPTS} "${fq}" > "${out_fq}"; then
        echo "  ERROR: filtlong failed on ${fq}, continuing with next file" >&2
        rm -f "${out_fq}"
        continue
    fi
done

echo
echo "Done. Filtered FASTQ files written to ${OUTPUT_DIR}/"
```
